**Catalyst Brands** is seeking a **Senior Financial Analyst** to support financial planning, forecasting, reporting, and business analysis for our **Lifestyle Brands** division, namely Aéropostale, Lucky Brand, and Nautica. This hybrid role is based in our **New York, NY** corporate office or our **Lyndhurst, NJ** finance office (preferred).

This position partners directly with Finance, Accounting, and Brand business leaders to evaluate performance across retail, e-commerce, and wholesale channels. You will analyze business drivers, explain financial variances, and deliver actionable insights that shape strategic business decisions.

The ideal candidate is an independent, self-starting professional who can own their work from end-to-end. You should blend proficient financial planning and analysis (FP&A) skills with a corporate accounting foundation, possessing an innate curiosity, a meticulous process for validating data, and the ability to translate operational activities into clear, strategic financial narratives.

Responsibilities:

* **Financial Planning & Analysis:** Drive and support annual budgeting, monthly forecasting, and long-range planning across retail, e-commerce, wholesale, and corporate operations. We are looking for hands-on partners who actively build and shape forecasts, not just compile reports.
* **Independent Ownership:** Take personal ownership of assigned business areas, forecasts, or recurring deliverables with limited supervision.
* **Analytical Modeling:** Build, maintain, and substantially improve sophisticated, driver-based financial models in Excel with clearly documented, reasonable assumptions that help the business make decisions.
* **Variance & Performance Analysis:** Analyze sales, gross margin, operating expenses (SG&A), and overall profitability against budget, forecast, and prior periods. Proactively investigate unexpected variances, identify underlying root causes, and recommend actionable solutions.
* **Accounting & General Ledger Integrity:** Analyze GL accounts and transaction-level details to validate monthly financial results and explain how accounting activity flows into financial statements. Partner closely with Accounting during month-end close to assess accrual needs and resolve discrepancies.
* **Commercial Analysis:** Partner cross-functionally with non-finance teams to understand operating plans and analyze the impacts of pricing strategies, product volume, category mix, and product costs on sales and gross margin performance across different brand channels.
* **Executive Presentation & Communication:** Partner cross-functionally to prepare and present clear financial results, forecasts, and strategic recommendations. You must be able to explain complex financial concepts clearly and confidently to both Finance and non-Finance business partners.

Qualifications:

**Required:**

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related quantitative field.
* **Experience:** 2 or more years of relevant, hands-on experience in FP&A, corporate finance, or a combination of corporate accounting and financial analysis.
* **Advanced Excel Capabilities:** High proficiency with advanced Excel features (including lookups, SUMIFS, index/match, pivot tables, and driver-based modeling) with a demonstrated ability to troubleshoot formulas.
* **Data Validation & Accuracy:** A structured, rigorous process for self-auditing, reconciling, and checking your own work for accuracy and completeness before presenting results to leadership.
* **Communication & Collaboration:** Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; a proven ability to work productively with non-finance partners to resolve issues and improve forecast accuracy.

**Preferred:**

* **Business Model Knowledge:** Solid working knowledge of retail (brick-and-mortar/e-commerce) and/or wholesale business models, including their unique financial drivers.
* **Industry Experience:** Prior finance or accounting experience within the apparel, footwear, retail, or consumer packaged goods (CPG) sectors.

**Catalyst Brands** is seeking a **Senior Financial Analyst** to support financial planning, forecasting, reporting, and business analysis for our **Lifestyle Brands** division, namely Aéropostale, Lucky Brand, and Nautica. This hybrid role is based in our **Lyndhurst, New Jersey** corporate office (preferred).

This position partners directly with Finance, Accounting, and Brand business leaders to evaluate performance across retail, e-commerce, and wholesale channels. You will analyze business drivers, explain financial variances, and deliver actionable insights that shape strategic business decisions.

The ideal candidate is an independent, self-starting professional who can own their work from end-to-end. You should blend proficient financial planning and analysis (FP&A) skills with a corporate accounting foundation, possessing an innate curiosity, a meticulous process for validating data, and the ability to translate operational activities into clear, strategic financial narratives.

Responsibilities:

* **Financial Planning & Analysis:** Drive and support annual budgeting, monthly forecasting, and long-range planning across retail, e-commerce, wholesale, and corporate operations. We are looking for hands-on partners who actively build and shape forecasts, not just compile reports.
* **Independent Ownership:** Take personal ownership of assigned business areas, forecasts, or recurring deliverables with limited supervision.
* **Analytical Modeling:** Build, maintain, and substantially improve sophisticated, driver-based financial models in Excel with clearly documented, reasonable assumptions that help the business make decisions.
* **Variance & Performance Analysis:** Analyze sales, gross margin, operating expenses (SG&A), and overall profitability against budget, forecast, and prior periods. Proactively investigate unexpected variances, identify underlying root causes, and recommend actionable solutions.
* **Accounting & General Ledger Integrity:** Analyze GL accounts and transaction-level details to validate monthly financial results and explain how accounting activity flows into financial statements. Partner closely with Accounting during month-end close to assess accrual needs and resolve discrepancies.
* **Commercial Analysis:** Partner cross-functionally with non-finance teams to understand operating plans and analyze the impacts of pricing strategies, product volume, category mix, and product costs on sales and gross margin performance across different brand channels.
* **Executive Presentation & Communication:** Partner cross-functionally to prepare and present clear financial results, forecasts, and strategic recommendations. You must be able to explain complex financial concepts clearly and confidently to both Finance and non-Finance business partners.

Qualifications:

**Required:**

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related quantitative field.
* **Experience:** 2 or more years of relevant, hands-on experience in FP&A, corporate finance, or a combination of corporate accounting and financial analysis.
* **Advanced Excel Capabilities:** High proficiency with advanced Excel features (including lookups, SUMIFS, index/match, pivot tables, and driver-based modeling) with a demonstrated ability to troubleshoot formulas.
* **Data Validation & Accuracy:** A structured, rigorous process for self-auditing, reconciling, and checking your own work for accuracy and completeness before presenting results to leadership.
* **Communication & Collaboration:** Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; a proven ability to work productively with non-finance partners to resolve issues and improve forecast accuracy.

**Preferred:**

* **Business Model Knowledge:** Solid working knowledge of retail (brick-and-mortar/e-commerce) and/or wholesale business models, including their unique financial drivers.
* **Industry Experience:** Prior finance or accounting experience within the apparel, footwear, retail, or consumer packaged goods (CPG) sectors.
* **Enterprise Systems:** Experience with enterprise systems and reporting tools, such as **Oracle, OneStream, or MicroStrategy**.

**What You Get**

If eligible, we offer a competitive benefits package including medical/dental/vision, term life insurance, paid vacation/holidays\*, and 401(k) with Company match. All associates are eligible for an associate discount on Catalyst Brands merchandise. For paid holidays, associates who are eligible for paid vacation (MTO) are also eligible for eight paid holidays during the calendar year. All store hourly associates scheduled to work on a designated holiday will receive additional compensation. \*For paid vacation days, as well as eligibility requirements for other benefits, please visit www.catalystbrandsbenefits.com

**About Catalyst**

Catalyst Brands reflects the bringing together the rich heritages of our brands with modern excitement and a new vision for success. Five iconic brands came together under a unified powerhouse portfolio to celebrate the essence of American style. We will leverage our rich history, resources and best-in-class industry talent to further build the success of our brands. At Catalyst we are united in one shared purpose: We exist to ignite America’s most beloved retail brands to make fashion accessible to all.

Working at Catalyst means joining a dedicated team of associates who are encouraged to be uniquely themselves in a safe, caring and welcoming environment. It is a place where careers prosper, accomplishments are celebrated and diversity flourishes. It’s a place that’s meant for you.

For more opportunities to join our team please visit our careers page.

Federal Reserve Bank of New YorkWhen you work at the New York Fed, you have the opportunity to make an impact in our communities and across the nation. **Our Unique Work:**

The FRBNY is exposed to credit risk through its provision of financial services to second district depository institutions and execution of market operations at the direction of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), as fiscal agent of the United States and for various official accountholders. More specifically, counterparty credit exposures arise from Discount Window lending, intraday extensions of credit through counterparties’ use of FRBNY payment systems and services, open market trading activities, Federal Reserve lending facilities and liquidity programs, and other activities. Trading activities include outright securities transactions, securities repurchase (repo) and reverse repo agreements, foreign exchange transactions, and foreign exchange swaps.

The Counterparty Credit Risk (CCR) team of the Markets Group is responsible for monitoring and assessing the credit risk of a diverse group of counterparties, identifying institutions that pose a heightened level of risk to the Bank, measuring the magnitude of such risk and implementing risk controls. CCR also participates in internal discussions concerning the trade-offs between policy benefits and risk exposure from extending credit and other topical financial issues.

**How You’ll Make an Impact as a Credit Risk Specialist:**

* Recommend and coordinate risk mitigation approaches for higher risk counterparties in collaboration with FRBNY Supervision, Financial Services, business teams, and other key stakeholders.
* Implement CCR’s failing bank process if needed, liaising with Legal, Supervision, Discount Window, Financial Services, other Reserve Banks, other regulators, and key stakeholders.

* Assist with investigations, including, but not limited to, gathering information, documentation, interviews, analysis, and reporting.

* Extensive use of computers.

Siemens Mobility North America seeks an experienced finance leader to head Finance and Performance Management (FPM) for its Rail Infrastructure (RI) business. The role provides an independent, forward-looking view of performance, serves as a trusted sparring partner to RI and Finance leadership, and connects the business unit with North America and global stakeholders.

You will lead the RI FPM team and own the coordination, consolidation, analysis and communication of financial performance, combining strong governance with commercial insight, constructive challenge and pragmatic decision support in a complex project and product environment.

**What You Will Accomplish**

* Drive fact-based performance management, translating financial and operational data into a clear view of results, outlook, risks, opportunities and required actions.
* Act as an independent, solution-oriented partner who challenges assumptions and explains trade-offs without taking over operational ownership.
* Build a coherent RI financial narrative that links drivers, financial statements and management priorities across segments and stakeholders.
* Develop a high-performing, collaborative FPM team that balances business proximity with common North America standards and continuous capability building.
* Advance process harmonization, digitalization, analytics and responsible AI to improve finance quality, speed and productivity.

**Key Responsibilities**

Business Partnership and Performance Management

* Serve as principal FPM partner to RI leadership and the primary RI interface to North America regional and global finance.
* Monitor key financial and operational indicators to spot trends, deviations, risks and opportunities early and turn them into decision-relevant insights.
* Objectively challenge forecasts, budgets, business cases and assumptions; develop scenarios, sensitivities and fact-based recommendations.
* Deliver concise executive analyses explaining what changed, why it matters, what remains uncertain and where action is needed.

Planning, Forecasting, Reporting and Financial Integrity

* Lead the RI annual budget, monthly forecast and management reporting processes, from calendars and inputs through consolidation, review, commentary and submission.
* Ensure a complete, accurate and consistent view of P&L, balance sheet and cash flow, with transparent bridges between actuals, forecast, budget and prior outlook.
* Challenge the plausibility of business and project inputs, investigate unusual entries and variances, and make material risks, opportunities and adjustments visible in the outlook.
* Partner with Accounting, Commercial Project Management, Operations and others to align close impacts, assumptions and the financial storyline, while keeping accountability for source data and business decisions clear.
* Escalate material performance, cash, balance-sheet, compliance or control issues promptly, with the evidence decision makers need.

Governance, Process Excellence and Digitalization

* Reinforce finance governance, internal-control and reporting requirements; support audit readiness and documentation of significant assumptions and judgments.
* Clarify responsibilities and interfaces across FPM, the business, Accounting, CPM, Operations and central functions to avoid duplication, ownership gaps and “shadow” controlling structures.
* Drive common North America FPM standards and best practices, allowing fit-for-purpose differences for RI business models and segments.
* Sponsor simplification, automation, analytics and digital-finance initiatives, including SAC, SAP, standardized templates and responsible AI-enabled workflows.
* Regularly assess the value, effort and control implications of recurring reports and processes, prioritizing improvements in insight, reliability or productivity.

Leadership and Talent Development

* Lead, coach and develop a diverse finance team with clear priorities, quality standards, responsibilities and development goals.
* Foster trust, candid communication, accountability, collaboration and continuous learning across locations and organizational boundaries.
* Balance business support, governance and capacity, focusing resources on material topics and ensuring resilient coverage of critical recurring processes.
* Contribute to the North America FPM leadership team and the OneFPM agenda, including talent development, succession planning and cross-business collaboration.

Scope and Accountability

FPM owns financial transparency, process coordination, consolidation, independent challenge and management insight; business and functional owners remain accountable for operational plans, source assumptions, corrective actions and final decisions. The Head of FPM RI keeps these interfaces explicit, surfaces material issues and ensures temporary support does not become a permanent transfer of ownership.

* Advanced proficiency with enterprise planning, reporting and analytics tools; experience with SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), SAP, data visualization, automation or AI-enabled finance workflows is an advantage.
* Experience in project-driven, infrastructure, transportation, or industrial businesses preferred.

The Department of City Planning (DCP) plans for the future of New York City, working to create thriving and dynamic neighborhoods with access to housing and jobs, resilient infrastructure, and a vibrant public realm. The Department engages communities to develop inclusive plans, expands housing access and economic opportunity, and plans for long-term sustainability.
  
  
DCP supports the City Planning Commission in its annual review of hundreds of land use applications. The Department also advises on citywide strategic and capital planning, analyzes data, conducts policy analysis, and creates open data and civic engagement tools. DCP is also the custodian of the official City Map, which designates streets, parks and other public places.
  
  
Department of City Planning offers staff meaningful opportunities to help shape the future of New York City and address some of its most pressing challenges. The Department values public service, collaboration, and creativity, and supports professional development. Learn more about DCP and view current job openings at www.nyc.gov/planning.
  
  
THE DIVISION
  
DCP’s Fiscal Division strives to improve the agency’s financial responsibility and operational effectiveness by providing information, analysis, and administrative and technical support to programs and divisions throughout the agency. The Fiscal team’s daily operations include, but are not limited to, procurement, grant management, accounting for both payments and receivables, budgeting and financial reporting.
  
  
Within DCP’s Fiscal Division, the Procurement Unit oversees the acquisition of goods and services for programs and teams across the agency, ensuring compliance with all applicable rules, laws, and mandates, including but not limited to Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, State and Federal procurement policies, NYC Comptroller Directives, Mayor’s Directives, Department of Citywide Administrative Services’ guidelines, and the City Charter. The Procurement Unit also manages the agency’s existing portfolio of contracts and DCP’s Minority and Women-Owned Enterprise (M/WBE) program.  
  
  
  
THE JOB
  
The Procurement team is seeking to hire a detail-oriented, highly motivated Procurement Analyst. Reporting to the Agency Chief Contracting Officer, the Procurement Analyst will be responsible for processing goods and services requests associated with various procurement methods for divisional needs while adhering to the City's PPB Rules, State and Federal Procurement requirements as applicable, and other Citywide Directives.
  
  
Under the supervision of the Agency Chief Contracting Officer, the selected candidate will be expected to assist the Procurement Division with an array of procurement functions and related tasks including but not limited to:
  
  

* Analyzing incoming procurement requests to determine appropriate procurement methods and reviewing request details for accuracy and adequacy.
* Supporting agency business units to meet purchasing needs efficiently and expeditiously, ensuring purchases are made in adherence with internal and external procurement policies and procedures.
* Working closely with Fiscal and business units to address funding needs for purchases and gathering technical requirements, respectively.

* Processing encumbrance increases and decreases as needed to facilitate payment processing and PO closeouts.
* Corresponding with vendors, obtaining quotes, responding to vendor inquiries, and troubleshooting order issues that may arise.
* Processing p-card purchases in compliance with Citywide P-Card Purchasing Policies and Requirements and performing monthly p-card reconciliations and reporting tasks.
* Supporting larger contract processes, such as preparing bid and/or solicitation specifications, facilitating contract registration, etc.
* Performing data entry, maintaining agency procurement trackers and records, and preparing various reports, etc.
* Performing other ad-hoc tasks as assigned.

#### **About GoodRec**

GoodRec makes it easy to play sports. Every week, more than **20,000 people** use GoodRec to play sports and meet people in person. We organized over **65,000 games in 2025** and are on track for more in 2026.

We’re building the platform for recreational sports — starting with pickup games and expanding into every way you play.

#### **About the Role**

We’re looking for an ambitious, entrepreneurial GTM to accelerate growth at Goodrec.You’ll work directly with the CEO on some of the company’s highest-priority growth problems.

One month you might launch a new growth channel. The next you might develop a strategic partnership, help crack a market, or test an entirely new business line.

Your job is simple: **find opportunities to grow GoodRec, prove they work, and turn them into scalable playbooks.**

#### **What You’ll Do**

* Launch and scale new growth initiatives
* Identify and test new business lines
* Develop strategic partnerships
* Test new acquisition and distribution channels
* Research markets, competitors, and growth opportunities
* Analyze customer and business data to find opportunities
* Talk directly with customers and partners
* Take ideas from **hypothesis test results scalable process**
* Build systems and processes where none exist today
* Work directly with the CEO and leadership team on company priorities

This isn’t a traditional sales role, and it isn’t a traditional strategy role. You’ll be expected to **figure out what will move the business forward and then make it happen.**

#### **Who We’re Looking For**

You have roughly **2–3 years of professional experience** and a track record of being excellent at what you do.

You:

* Are extremely smart, curious, and resourceful
* Have grit and can will things into existence
* Move quickly without needing much structure
* Think analytically but love execution
* Take ownership instead of waiting for direction
* Are comfortable selling, analyzing data, and building a process in the same day
* Communicate clearly and confidently
* Have high standards and care about details
* Want significantly more responsibility than most roles give someone early in their career
* Are excited by startups and building things from scratch

Experience in startups, consulting, growth, operations, business development, finance, or similar environments is helpful, but **we care much more about ability, trajectory, and evidence that you can get things done.**

#### **Why GoodRec**

* **Real ownership.** You’ll own projects that directly affect company growth.
* **Work directly with the CEO.** You’ll be involved in some of the most important problems and decisions in the company.
* **Build, don’t maintain.** You’ll constantly launch, test, and create things that don’t exist yet.
* **Meaningful scale.** We already connect 20,000+ people every week, but we believe GoodRec can become dramatically larger.
* **Grow with the company.** If you prove you can build and scale something, you’ll have the opportunity to own increasingly large parts of the business.

If you want a highly structured job with narrowly defined responsibilities, this probably isn’t the right role.

The Senior Affordable Rental Apartments (SARA) Program provides gap financing in the form of low interest loans to support the construction and renovation of affordable housing for seniors, 62+ years in age, with low incomes.

Homeless Housing Strategic Initiatives partners with DHS and other City Agencies on various homeless housing development initiatives including clusters conversion initiative, development of co-located permanent affordable housing with DHS shelters, and other development opportunities.

In 2023, the Capacity Accelerator Program (CAP) was launched to help the agency meet critical goals in its development portfolio. The CAP program’s core workstreams include staff training, the use of temporary staff to help meet key housing plan goals, the use of outside legal counsel to support transactions and other legal needs, and programmatic support to meet key preservation goals

· Serving as the primary point of contact for project sponsors, consultants, government agencies and other departments internal to HPD;

· Working with HPD’s legal department to collect and prepare loan closing documentation;

· Coordinating construction loan and syndication closings;

· Tracking construction status of projects post-closing and assisting in resolution of construction disputes;

· Coordinating processing of construction requisitions and change orders;

· Reporting on status of projects in predevelopment, construction and operation.

The Procurement Intelligence Analyst develops and delivers the analytics, market intelligence, performance reporting, and data insights that enable Enterprise Procurement to make informed, data-driven decisions. The role transforms procurement, supplier, financial, and operational data into actionable insights supporting category strategy, sourcing, Vendor Management, value realization, risk governance, and executive decision-making. Working collaboratively with Category Management, Vendor Management, Procurement Operations Hub, Finance, the Procurement Center of Excellence (COE), and business stakeholders, the role establishes trusted procurement reporting, spend visibility, supplier and vendor performance analytics, savings measurement, and market intelligence. The Procurement Intelligence Analyst also partners with the Procurement Digital Transformation Lead to advance automated reporting, AI-enabled analytics, and predictive insights as the organization builds a more digitally enabled procurement operating model.

**Duties & Responsibilities**

**Procurement Analytics, Performance & Executive Reporting**

* Develop, maintain, and continuously improve enterprise procurement dashboards, performance reports, and executive reporting that provide visibility into procurement value, operational performance, supplier performance, and strategic priorities.
* Establish and monitor procurement KPIs including savings and value realization, spend coverage, contract compliance, supplier performance, sourcing activity, cycle times, process efficiency, and stakeholder experience.
* Translate complex procurement data into clear insights, trends, and recommendations that support Procurement Leadership Team and executive decision-making.
* Produce recurring and ad hoc reporting for procurement leadership, governance forums, category reviews, Vendor Management reviews, and enterprise stakeholders.
* Ensure procurement reporting is accurate, timely, consistent, and supported by clearly defined metrics and trusted data sources.

**Spend, Category & Market Intelligence**

* Analyze enterprise spend across categories, suppliers, business units, and service areas to identify sourcing opportunities, demand trends, supplier concentration, and cost optimization opportunities.
* Develop category and supplier intelligence that supports category strategies, sourcing pipelines, negotiations, demand planning, and total cost of ownership analyses.
* Conduct market research and benchmarking across supplier markets, pricing trends, economic indicators, industry developments, and emerging technologies.
* Partner with Category Management to provide fact-based analytical support for category planning, supplier landscape assessments, business cases, and commercial recommendations.
* Maintain enterprise spend visibility and continuously improve spend classification, segmentation, and analytical usability.

**Supplier & Vendor Performance Intelligence**

* Develop and maintain supplier and vendor performance reporting, scorecards, and analytical views in support of Vendor Management and Category Management.
* Aggregate and analyze SLA, KPI, risk, issue, financial, and operational performance data to identify performance trends, emerging risks, and improvement opportunities.
* Provide analytical support for QBRs, executive business reviews, vendor governance meetings, supplier segmentation, and strategic account planning.
* Partner with Vendor Leads and business stakeholders to improve scorecard consistency, performance transparency, and actionable supplier insights.

**Allara** is a comprehensive women’s health provider that specializes in expert, longitudinal care that supports women through every life stage. Reporting to the VP of Engineering, this is a hands-on leadership role: in your first months you will be in the pipelines yourself, cleaning up our ETL, consolidating duplicated logic, and closing gaps in our source data. Over time you will define and drive the company's longer-term data strategy, set the standards the rest of the organization builds on, and grow the data function as Allara scales. This is a player-coach role, senior enough to own strategy and still happy to get the pipelines right yourself, and the hands-on work comes first.

**Location:** Hybrid (NYC). We value in-person collaboration and aim for at least three days per week in our NYC office, with flexibility as needed.

**Your Impact**
---------------

* Make Allara's data trustworthy, so every team can make decisions on numbers they believe.

* **Close source-data gaps.** Map what we collect against what the business needs and close the gaps across our systems.
* **Make the data trustworthy.** Stand up data-quality testing, monitoring, and alerting.
* **Establish one source of truth.** Define a canonical metric and semantic layer

* **Own AI-ready data.** Own the shared, AI-ready data layer and the canonical terminology definitions and skills that power AI-assisted analysis across departments.
* **Build the team.** Hire, mentor, and lead the data engineering function over time, setting the technical bar and the practices the team works by.

* 8+ years in data engineering or analytics engineering, including direct, recent ownership of production ETL and warehouse modeling.

* Strong data modeling fundamentals and a real bias toward a single source of truth.
* Experience designing data governance and handling sensitive data, with comfort around security and access control in a regulated environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Healthcare or HIPAA experience, including familiarity with EMR data (FHIR) and claims.
* Experience with D2C growth metrics
* Experience with Amplitude and product event taxonomy, and enabling AI or LLM-assisted analytics such as semantic layers, metric catalogs, or Claude skills.
* Experience building and managing a data team at a high-growth startup (Series B to D).

*Having these would be advantageous over candidates lacking these qualifications and would potentially allow the candidate to have a greater and/or more immediate impact on the role.*

*Actual compensation will be determined based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to: candidate experience, location, education, certifications, and skill set. In addition to base salary, our total compensation package includes equity, comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision), generous paid time off, and additional wellness and professional development perks.*

Align is seeking a Director, Talent and Culture to lead and evolve our Talent and Culture function as we grow. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this role connects our business objectives, culture, and professional experience, and partners with executive leadership to design and implement talent, career development, and culture strategies.

A core priority of this role is building and administering a structured career management and coaching program, modeled on a guidance counselor, so every professional across our lines of business understands their options, has a development plan, and sees a path to grow at Align. The ideal candidate is a people-first leader with a strategic approach to systems, data, and technology, and the appetite to grow into broader People leadership as Align scales.

* This position works out of our Midtown Manhattan office.
* This is a full-time position offering full benefits, a base salary in the $170,000–$200,000 range (commensurate with experience), and performance-based bonuses.

* **Leadership & Strategy:** Build and scale a high-performing Talent and Culture function in partnership with executive leadership.

ABOUT THE CAMPAIGN FINANCE BOARD
  
  
The Campaign Finance Board is a nonpartisan, independent city agency that empowers New Yorkers to have a greater impact on their elections. Our mission is to make local democracy more open, transparent, and equitable by removing barriers to participation.
  
  
We make it easier for New Yorkers to vote, meaningfully support candidates for city office, and run for office themselves. NYC Votes, our voter engagement initiative, meets people where they are to share trustworthy election information and help New Yorkers make a plan to vote. We publish the citywide Voter Guide, which delivers information about candidates directly to voters’ doors. Our public matching funds program ensures small contributions can make a big difference, allowing regular people to run for office by relying on the support of other regular people, not just wealthy donors and special interests. And we lift the veil on how candidates raise and spend money, increasing transparency and accountability in local government.
  
  
We believe that when every New Yorker is empowered to participate meaningfully in elections, candidates will better reflect the communities they serve, elected leaders will be more accountable to the public, and New Yorkers will have a democracy they can truly trust.
  
  
ABOUT THE UNIT
  
  
The People and Engagement Division is responsible for the agency's systems, policies, and resources that work to shape engagement and the employee experience at the CFB.
  
  
The division encompasses multiple units including the Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) unit, People and Culture unit, the Learning and Development unit, and the Labor Relations, Timekeeping, Payroll, Benefits and Compliance unit. Its work spans the entire employee lifecycle; from recruitment and selection, onboarding, to workplace culture, succession planning, learning and development, and organizational restructuring. The Division also manages employee and labor relations, payroll, timekeeping, offboarding, and benefits administration. Together we work to build people systems that allow for a positive employee experience and workplace culture.
  
  
The People & Culture Unit serves as an internal strategic partner dedicated to supporting employees and advancing the agency across every stage of the employee lifecycle. The unit delivers comprehensive HR-based solutions in the areas of talent operations, employee growth and development, and organizational culture. We are looking for a full-time COO to join us as the senior-most business leader in the firm. We run on EOS, and you will serve as our Integrator, reporting directly to the two founding partners.  
Here is the honest context. We built this firm’s operations ourselves, and the firm has outgrown the way we built them. We have strong department leaders, a growing brand, and some very good years in front of us. What we don't have is one person who is fully engaged in driving the business forward: someone who identifies the priorities, brings us recommendations, and gets the team executing without either founder having to keep pushing things along (or getting in the way). Everything else in this description is detail. That is the job.  
  
**Why Be the COO at Chaffin Luhana?**  
**Run the business.** You will run the whole business, not a slice of it. Marketing, intake, client experience, finance, people, and technology all report through this seat, and you will work directly with the two founders on where the firm goes next.  
**Help shape what comes next.** AI, management services organizations (MSOs), and changing client expectations are creating new choices for law firms. title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
Our client runs the compliant system of record you build on to move, store, and grow money. Launch financial products your customers love. We provide the financial primitives, licenses, and compliance, and our forward deployed team gets you live in two weeks. Under the hood, fiat and blockchain run as one system. Their customers never see any of it. Money comes in, money goes out, and it just gets there.

**The Role**

Our customers don't just call our APIs. They build their products on us. Their balances, their payment operations, their compliance state. Which means our business succeeds exactly as far as theirs do. Forward Deployed Engineering is the team that makes that true, one customer at a time.

You'll report to our CTO and embed with one strategic customer at a time, the enterprises building their products where we're investing deepest. You'll understand their business, their constraints, and their pain points better than anyone, and then you'll build what their launch needs.

Here's a concrete example. A global payouts customer is expanding into a new market where we don't yet have local account infrastructure. You scope the requirements with their engineering team, then build the virtual account infrastructure, in our core codebase, that their launch depends on. When it ships, it's not a one-off. It becomes a core product that we sell to the next ten customers.

That's the defining property of this role. This is not a services role, and it's not technical support. You're a product engineer whose roadmap comes from a live customer instead of a planning doc. Everything you build lands in the core platform, and the best of it becomes product the whole company resells. Engagements are scoped at contract time. You're delivering what we've committed to, not absorbing unbounded requests. But within that scope, the what, the why, and the how are yours to figure out with the customer.

**What You'll Do**

* **Deploy into customer contexts.** Iterate daily with your customer's engineering and operations teams, mostly over Zoom and Slack, with some travel to spend real time on site.
* **Scope the build with the customer.** You're not handed a spec. You work out what to build and why with the customer directly, paired with a deployment strategist who owns the commercial side.
* **Build across the full stack.** TypeScript and React, NestJS with Postgres and Prisma, and AWS (SQS, SNS, Lambda). New account infrastructure, blockchain integrations, API endpoints, compliance workflows, whatever the launch requires.
* **Generalize the bespoke.** Identify patterns across implementations and work with product to turn engagement output into first-class platform features.
* **Prototype fast, ship carefully.** Rapid iteration against live customer workflows, accepting some throwaway work and making sure what isn't throwaway gets productized properly, all while debugging production issues in real time, sometimes with the customer watching.
* **Design for correctness and auditability.** This is money-movement infrastructure. Edge cases have real consequences, and you think about failure modes before they happen.
* **Communicate crisply** with customer engineers, operators, founders, and finance leaders, and with our own product leads, whose pods your work must generalize into.

**Who You Are**

* **You're a builder first.** We're flexible on tenure. We'll hire a scrappy engineer straight out of school or a seasoned customer-facing engineer. We're not flexible on the bar. You ship production-grade, full-stack work, and you have something you've built to prove it.
* **You're AI-native.** Agentic tools are how you already build, and we'll ask you to show us.
* **You're energized by customers, not shielded from them.** You're comfortable operating directly with an enterprise engineering team, under ambiguity, where the requirements are yours to discover.
* **You're obsessed with correctness and resilience.** You love a good state machine. You think carefully about what happens when things go wrong, because with money they can't.
* **Strong pluses.** Payments and fintech infrastructure experience, blockchain and stablecoin integration work, and a forward-deployed or solutions architect background where you *built* rather than just configured.

**What Success Looks Like**

* Your customer launches on time, on our rails, and their volume ramps because what you built works.
* The infrastructure you shipped for one customer is now core product being sold to the next ten.
* Your customer's engineering team treats you as one of their own, and our team trusts what you merge.
* You've defined, alongside our CTO, what "forward deployed" means.
* You're an early member of a function we're building the company around.

**How We Work**

We run on three principles:

* **2% better, every day.** One percent for yourself, one percent for the people around you.
* **Telos.** From the Greek word telos, meaning not just done but fulfilled. Everyone here is focused on one mission and knows each other's Telos.
* **Build.** Embody the builder's mindset. Make things, solve problems, and have fun doing it.

Bilt is the membership for where you live.

  
  

What started as a way to reward people on their largest expense has turned into an ecosystem connecting our members, property managers and local merchants.

- Establish Finance-specific AI guidelines aligned to enterprise AI policy, covering data handling, model risk, SOX implications, auditability, and human-in-the-loop requirements.

- Provide Executive-ready updates on Finance & Accounting AI portfolio, outcomes, and emerging risks.

 Payroll Planning & Budget Ownership 
 • Own the full store payroll cycle, from setting annual budgets to forecasting hours, wage rates and dollars each month.
 • Partner with FP&A to track payroll expense, explain variances and respond to sales and workload trends so stores stay on budget.

 • Own labor KPIs (sales per labor hour, labor % to sales, overtime, schedule accuracy) and keep reporting accurate and easy to use for every level of leadership.
 • Deliver ad-hoc analysis as needed, from new store performance to year-over-year comparisons.
 Efficiency & Partnership

 • Partner cross-functionally with Compensation, Finance, HR, Payroll, Communications and New Store Opening teams, and support broader Store Operations initiatives.

title: Clinical Research Associate II
description:
Advance AbbVie's pipeline by striving for excellence in clinical research, turning science into medicine for our patients and leveraging new advanced capabilities to drive industry leading performance.
Partners with the investigator and site staff for meaningful and effective engagements positioning AbbVie as the choice in clinical trials.
Focus on site clinical research that ensures appropriate conduct of the trial while driving improvement in data integrity, compliance, overall study performance and customer experience.
 Responsibilities
- Considered as the primary point of contact for the investigative site. High level of competency or experience in providing contextual information on the clinical trials, connects stakeholder to the investigative sites and strengthens AbbVie’s positioning.
- Aligns, trains and motivates the site staff and principal investigator on the goals of the clinical trial program, protocol and patient treatment principles for the trial ensuring a trusted partnership.
- Conducts site evaluation, site training, routine, and site closure monitoring activities with compliance to the protocol and monitoring plans, in accordance with applicable regulations, Good Clinical Practices (GCPs), ICH Guidelines, AbbVie Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and quality standards, ensuring safety and protection of study subjects.
- Advanced understanding of site engagement and ability to customize site engagement strategy for assigned study (ies). Gather local/site insights and utilize site engagement tools such as the Customer Relationship Management (CRM) tool, to report/track progress and measure impact of that strategy.
- Advanced level of competency connecting the study protocol, scientific principles and clinical trial requirements to the day-to-day clinical trial execution activities. Evaluate and ensure effective recruitment and retention techniques/plans based on the patient disease journey.
Develop solid knowledge of therapeutic area, asset and clinical landscape / patient journey to enable successful patient recruitment and overall protocol compliance.
- Possesses experienced level of competency to mentor and train less experienced CRAs on various aspects of work and provides input into their development.
May participate in global/local task forces and initiatives. Responsible for activities as assigned by manager.
- Responsible for continuous risk-assessment proactively, and in collaboration with Central Monitoring team, monitor activities conducted by clinical sites to detect early overall study performance or patient safety issues.
- Advanced ability to think critically to resolve site risk signals while having robust understanding of site processes to drive study execution. Ensures preventative and corrective action plans are put into place, as needed, to mitigate risk and promote compliance using a customer centric approach.
- Identifies, evaluates and recommends new/potential investigators/sites on an on going basis. Potential sites may be identified through networking or internal AbbVie requests to assist in the placement of planned clinical studies with qualified investigators.
- Ensures quality of data submitted from study sites and assures timely submission of data, including appropriate reporting and follow-up for all safety events by site personnel.
Ensures audit and regulatory inspection readiness at assigned clinical site at all times.
Manages investigator payments as per executed contract obligations, as applicable.

- Appropriate tertiary qualification in health related disciplines (Medical, Scientific, Nursing) preferred.
- Minimum of 1 year of clinically related experience, of which a period of 6 months is required in clinical research monitoring of investigational drug or device trials. Familiar with risk‐based monitoring approach, onsite and offsite monitoring.
- Knowledge of appropriate therapeutic area indications is preferred with the ability to understand and apply scientific concepts as they relate to the conduct of clinical trials.
- Advanced knowledge on existing and emerging local regulatory and legal requirements, ICH/GCP Guidelines and applicable policies.
- Demonstrate strong cross-functional collaboration skills among internal and external stakeholders.
- Demonstrate strong planning and organizational skills and the ability to work effectively and efficiently in a dynamic environment with competing projects and deadlines.
- Advanced ability to leverage technology, tools and resources to provide customer centric support based on the health of the site.
- Strong interpersonal skills with excellent written, verbal, active listening and presentation skills, with ability to establish and leverage site relationships and trusted partnerships through engagement, motivation, and training.
- Ability to use functional expertise with appropriate guidance, leverage critical thinking skills and apply good judgement to address clinical site issues.
- Acts with integrity in accordance with AbbVie code of business conduct and leadership values. Self-motivated individual focused on delivering timely and quality outcomes in a fast-paced environment.

This range may be modified in the future. ​

title: Senior Financial Analyst, Central Finance
description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role:

Crusoe is looking for a Senior Financial Analyst, Central Finance to support a variety of corporate finance initiatives, solving critical finance, strategy, and operations-related problems across the organization. This role offers a unique opportunity to work across teams and see firsthand how a fast-growing business operates — a great platform for learning how to operationalize change at scale. This is a highly visible role that interacts regularly with executive management, and requires someone comfortable moving fluidly across Finance, Corporate Development, Treasury, and business groups.



The ideal candidate is highly analytical, detail-oriented, and comfortable multi-tasking in a results-oriented, fast-paced environment. This is a full-time, exempt position.



What You'll Be Working On:

 - Financial Modeling & Analysis — Build and maintain robust financial models for corporate planning, budgeting, and cash flow forecasting; perform sensitivity, scenario, and variance analysis to evaluate performance and inform decision-making.

 - Planning & Forecasting — Drive the monthly forecasting and annual budgeting processes by partnering with business unit finance teams to gather inputs, consolidate actuals and forecast data, and deliver accurate, timely financial plans aligned with corporate targets.

 - Performance Management Reporting — Create and support monthly executive team reports, board materials, and ad-hoc analyses, building clear, actionable performance narratives for leadership.

 - Systems & Data Management — Own and manage the company’s planning platform, ensuring data integrity, availability, and accuracy for financial reporting and analysis; identify opportunities to integrate AI and automation to enhance forecasting and reporting capabilities.

 - Cross-Functional Partnership — Collaborate with Cloud, Digital Infrastructure, Accounting, and other teams to ensure Finance model assumptions reflect the latest business inputs and meet reporting and control standards.



What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - 2-4 years of experience in financial planning & analysis, investment banking, treasury, or corporate finance required.

 - Excellent skills in financial modeling and forecasting.

 - Strong interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills.

 - Team player who can work well independently and with limited direction.

 - Working knowledge of accounting principles and financial statements.

 - Detail-orientation with a focus on accuracy and precision.



Bonus Points

 - MBA or CFA designation.

 - Client or industry experience in Technology, Data Center Infrastructure, Cloud, or Energy.



Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $130,000 - $160,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.



Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

title: Senior Associate, Financial Planning & Analysis
description:
Over the last 20 years, Ares’ success has been driven by our people and our culture. Today, our team is guided by our core values – Collaborative, Responsible, Entrepreneurial, Self-Aware, Trustworthy – and our purpose to be a catalyst for shared prosperity and a better future. Through our recruitment, career development and employee-focused programming, we are committed to fostering a welcoming and inclusive work environment where high-performance talent of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives can build careers within this exciting and growing industry. 
 Job Description 
 Ares is seeking an experienced Associate to join its Global Corporate Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A) team in New York and serve as the dedicated FP&A partner for the evergreen funds within the Infrastructure Equity strategy. The associate will own the fund-level financial models and provide integrated planning, forecasting, performance analysis, and decision support in close partnership with the Infrastructure Equity team and finance stakeholders.
 The ideal candidate combines advanced financial modeling skills and strong accounting and financial statement knowledge with the ability to translate complex fund and portfolio data into clear insights and recommendations.
 Primary functions and essential responsibilities
 Support the FP&A VP and build effective relationships across Infrastructure Equity investment team, fund and corporate accounting, tax, divisional CFO organization, and technology teams.
 Planning, Forecasting & Performance Analysis 
- Support the annual budget, periodic forecast, and long-range planning processes for the evergreen funds within the Infrastructure Equity strategy.
- Integrate investment-level assumptions with fund-level forecasts, including investment performance, cash flows, liquidity, leverage, NAV, earnings, distributions, and investor returns.
- Analyze actual and forecasted performance, identify key business drivers and risks, and clearly explain variances against prior forecasts, budgets, underwriting cases, and realized results.
- Translate fund performance and model outputs into relevant management fee, incentive fee, and other earnings forecasts used in divisional and consolidated Ares planning and reporting.

WHY WE EXIST

Your car and your home are your most important assets, yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every part of the journey — buy/sell, insurance, maintenance, repairs — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

Jerry.ai http://Jerry.ai is building the first app to manage it all. We started with car insurance in 2019, became one of the top 3 brokers in the U.S., then added driving insights, diagnostics, and a repair marketplace.

We’ve reached 5M+ customers, raised $240M+, and scaled revenue 70X. We’re now expanding into adjacent verticals (e.g. home, motorcycle, RV, etc) to become the one-stop-shop for all your physical assets.




WHY WE’RE HIRING

Jerry is expanding into several new markets at the same time. Capital allocation is now one of the most consequential decisions we make: each dollar committed to a new product line, a marketing channel, or a headcount is a dollar not available elsewhere.

We are hiring a Strategic Finance Manager, reporting to our VP of Finance, to build the analysis those decisions rest on. You will own the operating model and the planning cycle, partner with functional leaders across the company, and work closely with the CFO and the founders.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN

The operating core is the model, the planning cadence, and the spend discipline the company runs on. Alongside it, you are the analytical partner on new opportunities — the products, verticals, channels and partnerships we are deciding whether to back. And over your first year or two, as our newer products scale and the audience for our numbers widens beyond the people who already know the business, the reporting itself has to reach a standard that holds up to outside diligence.



Own the operating model and forecast cycle:

 - Own Jerry’s driver-based operating model for the base business and expand it as we launch new insurance products and business lines.

 - Run the annual budget and long-range planning process end to end — cadence, assumptions, stakeholder inputs, and the consolidated plan the executive team commits to.

 - Own the monthly and quarterly forecast cycle and variance analysis: Once Accounting closes the books, explain what moved against plan and prior period, why it moved, and what it means for the forecast.

 - Write the executive narrative: Translate the financial results into clear business insights for the CFO, the founders, the board, and our investors, at a standard that survives external diligence.

 - Lead monthly business reviews: Work with functional leaders and turn what the numbers show into the business decisions that need to be made.

 - Support the team in evaluating and implementing a planning system: Assess the options, make the recommendation, and own the rollout.

Build the financial case for new opportunities

 - Build the financial model for new product, vertical, channel or partnership: Size the market, model the economics, evaluate capital commitment and return profile.

 - Read results back against the case: Once something is live, compare the actual economics to what we underwrote and carry the lesson into the next decision. Monitor product and channel economics including CAC and payback, policy retention and lifetime value, contribution margin etc.

 - Support corporate development: Capital markets and investor workstreams through diligence, modeling, and transaction analysis as the need arises.

 - Frame build, buy or partner decisions: help refine the frameworks we use to compare the options and the return profile of each.

Underwrite vendor spend:

 - Build the business case before a commitment is made, support negotiation on terms, and give budget owners the visibility to manage their own numbers.




WHO YOU ARE

 - Accurate under deadline: Your numbers are right the first time, and they stay right when the deadline compresses. You check your own work before anyone else has to.

 - Picks the right question: No one hands you the workstream. You decide which analysis will actually change a decision, and leave the rest alone.

 - Direct communicator: You form a view, communicate it directly, and revise it when the evidence changes.

 - Executive-ready output: What you produce can go in front of the founders or the board without a rewrite — clear, precise, and honest about what the numbers do and do not show.

 - Owner: You take ownership of outcomes and are comfortable building process where none exists yet.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 4+ years of relevant experience, ideally combining 2+ years at a reputable investment bank, corporate development group, or private equity firm with 2+ years in strategic finance or FP&A at a high-growth company.

 - A bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, or a similarly quantitative field.

 - Strong financial modeling skills: driver-based operating models, three-statement mechanics, scenario and sensitivity analysis, and a working command of accounting concepts and GAAP.

 - Experience with unit economics in a consumer or marketplace business, including CAC, LTV, payback, cohort retention, and contribution margin.

 - A track record of translating complex analysis into a clear narrative for an executive or investor audience.

 - Startup or high-growth experience strongly preferred, including building financial processes from scratch.

 - Hands-on fluency with AI tools for analysis, research, and workflow automation.

Nice to have:

 - Insurance, insurtech, fintech, or marketplace experience;

 - CFA certification;

 - vendor negotiation or procurement exposure;

 - finance tech stack experience (NetSuite, Ramp, planning tools).

 One thing makes this role different from similar seats at established platforms: nothing here is inherited. The operating model, the metric definitions, the launch methodology, the planning cadence - they do not exist yet. You will design them from a blank page, pressure-test them against a business that is scaling extremely fast, and then run them with rigor. You sit at the interface of Sales, Product, platform, Capacity, Finance and Marketing.
 What you'll do 
 Build the GTM operating system — from the ground up 
- Design Nscale's GTM operating model: account engagement standards, funnel design, pipeline stages and forecasting methodology - and the execution standards that make them stick
- Define, instrument and operationalize the core GTM metric set - pipeline health, deal velocity, forecast accuracy, capacity sold-forward at energization, utilization on landed accounts - and build the executive dashboards on top of it

- A clear point of view on how enterprise and AI-native accounts should be engaged, and the ability to influence senior sales leaders and executives without direct authority
- Written for and presented to senior executives - you can produce the readout leadership reads and hold the room with Product, Finance and Engineering counterparts
- Exceptional analytical skills rooted in data but never without actionable insight: SQL, sophisticated modeling in Sheets or Excel, and experience with BI tools (Looker, BigQuery or similar)

You will work with infrastructure teams and project partners, education providers, and local Community Engagement Leads to understand workforce needs and help education and training providers prepare people for these jobs of the future.

You will build partnerships with local community colleges, technical schools, universities, and union apprenticeship programs from the ground up. description:
REVENUE OPERATIONS LEAD

Location: USA Remote / San Francisco, CA · Full-Time

 


ABOUT ANDROMEDA

Andromeda is a market and infrastructure platform to buy, sell, and operate compute.

We believe demand for compute will grow exponentially. So fast that a handful of vertically integrated providers won't be able to scale across operations, capital, supply chains, and politics to serve it. The result is a massive wave of fragmentation, with AI factories of every shape and size coming to market to fill this demand. Our job is to enable all of that fragmented compute to flow through one platform, delivering reliable capacity to model builders, research labs, and inference providers when they need it. We believe every spare electron should be made productive for AI and we're building the platform that makes that possible.


We sit at the center of three forces:

 - Companies that need reliable, high-performance compute fast

 - A fragmented global supply of GPUs across hyperscalers, neoclouds, and independent data centers

 - Capital, risk, and operational complexity that most teams are not equipped to manage

When we succeed, trillions of dollars of compute will flow through Andromeda. Builders get capacity when they need it. Providers get a reliable way to monetize, operate, and finance infrastructure at scale. Capital gets an easy way to deploy, hedge, and underwrite.

In five years, Andromeda won't just participate in the AI infrastructure market. We will shape it.

 


THE ROLE

This is a chance to join Andromeda as our first Revenue Operations Lead — a strategic partner to Sales, Customer Success, and leadership as we scale a GPU compute market moving through its first real step-change in revenue. You'll own the operating system behind the number: pipeline hygiene, forecasting, deal desk process, supply administration, and the connective tissue between sales, supply, legal, and finance.

 

There's no playbook to inherit here. Our systems don't yet talk to each other the way they should, our routing and RACI are still being formalized, and the revenue org is being built from scratch. If you're an analytical operator who thrives in unstructured environments and loves bringing order to chaos, this role gives you the room to build it — and a path to leading revenue operations as the team grows.

 

What You’ll Do 

● GTM tech stack: Own and optimize HubSpot (current CRM) — field standardization, data hygiene cadence, and integrations so deal blockers, supply status, and pipeline data actually stay in sync.

● Forecasting & reporting infrastructure: Build and maintain the dashboards and forecast rollups sales leadership relies on for weekly deal reviews — pipeline health, coverage, and revenue performance against target.

● Deal desk & process design: Run the routing logic between strategic and velocity deals, own the RACI as the org scales, and close the sequencing gaps between customer and provider contracting.

● Planning & compensation: Partner with sales leadership and finance on capacity planning, quota design, and comp modeling

● AI-driven efficiency: Identify where AI tools and workflows can cut manual work out of reporting, forecasting, and deal ops — you'll be operating inside a team that already runs a lot of its own workflow through AI, and should be looking to extend that.

● Cross-functional glue: Sit at the intersection of sales, supply/ops, legal, and finance. Identify friction points in our business and get us unblocked.

 

What We’re Looking For

● Experience: 5+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or Business Operations at a high-growth B2B company — ideally one with usage-based, capacity-based, or infrastructure pricing (compute, cloud, hosting).

● CRM fluency: Hands-on CRM ownership at scale — you've built field architecture, workflows, and hygiene process, not just pulled reports.

● Systems thinking with a long-term view: You design for what a process looks like six months after go-live, not just whether it works on day one.

● Builder, not maintainer: You've owned a process end to end — comp calculations, forecasting model, deal desk — not just supported someone else running it. Comfortable standing up infrastructure from scratch.

● High agency, high ambiguity tolerance: This role sits across sales, supply, legal, and finance, and the "way it's supposed to work" is still being defined in real time.

● Directness: Shows up with proposals instead of open questions, and is comfortable being the source of truth on numbers people won't always like — forecast misses, comp disputes.

 

Not A Fit

● Wants a mature, fully-built RevOps org with existing playbooks to execute.

● Needs significant structure or direction to prioritize their own work.

● Uncomfortable owning and delivering hard numbers directly and without spin.

 

Strong Candidates May Have

● Domain experience: Time at a hyperscaler, GPU cloud, or other high-performance compute environment — familiarity with large-scale AI training and inference infrastructure is a real edge here, not a nice-to-have.

● Scaling experience: Built deal desk or forecasting process at a company scaling through a step-change in revenue (e.g., ~$200M to $700M+ run-rate).

● Technical depth: SQL or scripting fluency for reporting that goes beyond what the CRM natively supports.

 

Why You’ll Love It Here

● Ground floor of a category-defining company in the fastest-growing infrastructure market in tech

● High-leverage seat — this role designs the operating system for revenue, not just reports on it.

● Competitive compensation: + meaningful equity

● Comprehensive benefits: for you and your dependents, including healthcare, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k), and unlimited PTO

About the Role

Industrious signs new landlord partnerships every year, and the number is growing as our business development team expands. Before any of those deals move forward, someone has to check that it holds together: that the assumptions are sound, that the start date, budgets, rent, pricing, and returns all track, and that the figures from design and construction have carried through correctly. As a Real Estate Associate on our Real Estate Transactions team that will be your job!



You will underwrite assigned deals in Excel, explain what drives their returns, and flag where a deal is tight, whether on pricing, occupancy, or CapEx. Our business development colleagues make the call on whether a deal goes ahead, and your analysis is what they rely on to make it well. You will work with Design, Construction, Finance, and other teams to make sure every number is right, supporting several business development colleagues as deal flow shifts.



Our approach to underwriting is different from a traditional real estate shop, and we will teach it to you. In your first few months you will get close review and clear guidance while you learn how we work. You will also join at a good time: the team is growing, new roles are being added, and we are underwriting a new product, so there is real room to learn, ask questions, and grow with us.



Success here means accurate work. The team trusts your numbers, your flags are clear, and any mistake you make happens once, not twice.



What Might Your Day Look Like

Your morning starts with a new deal from one of our business development colleagues. You go through the model piece by piece: the start date, the budget, the rent and revenue share assumptions, the cash flows, the IRR, and the margin the location is expected to earn per rentable square foot. The returns look fine at first, but pricing is tighter than it seems, so you note it clearly with the number that would need to change.



Late morning, updated figures arrive from Design and Construction. You check that they have flowed into the model correctly. One CapEx figure does not match the construction budget, so you confirm the right number with the construction team before it goes any further.



In the afternoon, you walk your business development colleague through the deal: what the returns look like, where the risk sits, and which assumptions matter most. They decide what happens next. Then priorities shift, and another colleague needs support on a deal heading to Investment Committee, so you move over and check that every figure in the review material ties back to the underwriting.



Before you wrap up, you update your trackers and checklists so the team knows where every deal you are supporting stands.



What You Will Own

 - Underwrite assigned deals in Excel, checking every assumption and making sure each component, from start date and budgets to pricing and IRR, tracks.

 - Flag where a deal is tight, on pricing, occupancy, CapEx, OpEx, rent, or revenue share, and where it may need more support.

 - Make sure figures from Design, Construction, and Finance carry through accurately into the deal.

 - Support deal reviews and Investment Committee materials with numbers that hold up to scrutiny.

 - Support several business development colleagues across their deal flow, moving between priorities as needs change.

 - Keep the trackers and checklists that help the team stay accurate as deal volume grows.
   
   

You Will Love This Role If...

 - You are curious about real estate and want to understand why a deal works, not just what the model says.

This Role Is Probably Not for You If...

 - You find detailed checking draining. This role covers a high volume of deals, and the standard is accuracy every time.

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.



Role Purpose

Neko Health is expanding into the US market, and this role is being created to make sure staffing, shift structures, and labor resources keep pace with that growth without compromising service levels or cost efficiency.

This is first and foremost a strategic, data-driven role. The Workforce Management Lead will analyze and understand Neko's labour performance and measuring end to end — from raw operational data through to the strategic staffing and cost decisions that data should drive — and will explore AI-enabled ways to structure and organize the workforce, rather than defaulting to manual or legacy scheduling methods. This role is also expected to contribute to day-to-day rota scheduling support.



What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

Strategic labour analytics (lead priority)

 - Own end-to-end analysis of Neko's labour performance and metrics — productivity, utilization, cost per labor hour, and labor waste — from raw data through to a strategic read leadership can act on, not just a monitoring dashboard.

 - Develop short- and long-term labor forecasts using historical data, seasonality trends, and business growth projections.

 - Provide insights and recommendations to leadership on staffing and operational decisions, including staffing adjustments during demand surges (e.g., flu season).

AI-enabled workforce design

 - Explore AI-enabled approaches to structuring and organizing the workforce — e.g., using AI/ML methods to improve shift-pattern design, coverage modeling, or forecasting accuracy — rather than relying solely on manual or legacy methods.

 - Identify and pilot specific opportunities where AI or automation can materially improve staffing efficiency or decision quality.

Data & systems build

 - Design and build the forecasting models, dashboards, and staffing tools this role depends on, rather than operating tools built by another team.

 - Structure the right tech stack for scheduling, time tracking, and leave management, and identify automation opportunities within it.

Cross-functional coordination

 - Work with HR, Operations, and Medical Operations to manage absenteeism, overtime, and productivity gaps, using the labour-analytics work above to inform those conversations.

Day-to-day: rota scheduling support

 - Support rota scheduling and shift coverage across clinics in multiple geographies, ensuring the right staffing mix across shifts (days, evenings, weekends).

 - Support shift bid processes and shift rotations to optimize coverage and employee satisfaction.



Minimum Qualifications

 - Proven experience of building a workforce forecasting model, staffing tool, or scheduling dashboard from scratch — not only configured or operated one built by another team or vendor.

 - Experience applying AI or machine-learning methods to workforce planning, forecasting, or scheduling problems.

 - Has owned workforce planning and labour-metrics analysis across multiple sites

 - Strong analytical skills with proficiency in data tools (e.g., Excel, Tableau, SQL) and workforce planning systems.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.



Preferred Experience

 - Background in any shift-based, multi-site industry (e.g., retail, logistics/warehousing, aviation, , hospitality, manufacturing) is valued as much as healthcare experience.

- Producing detailed Net Asset Value (“NAV”) analysis on a monthly basis and NAV forecasts

- Interfacing with portfolio investment counterparties, financing counterparties, and other external partners
- Monitoring contract compliance including preparation of key metrics such as Debt Service Coverage Ratios

- Preparation and presentation of analyses and reporting materials to internal and external stakeholders
- Collaborating closely with the Investment team, FP&A team and other internal stakeholders to ensure accurate reporting and compliance with financial regulations
 Qualifications: 
- Bachelor's degree or international equivalent, along with relevant work experience

US Finance Data Contributor – AI Research (Remote, Task-Based) 
 About Prolific 
 Prolific is not just another player in the AI space – we are building the biggest pool of quality human data in the world.
 Over 35,000 AI developers, researchers, and organizations use Prolific to gather data from paid study participants with a wide variety of experiences, knowledge, and skills.
 The Opportunity 
 We are looking for US-based participants aged 18+ to take part in a paid research project using real-world financial data to help train AI models.
 No finance background is required. The task is remote and flexible and takes approximately 1–2 hours for most participants.
 Tasks 
- Download genuine financial records from your own accounts.
- Provide data from 5 required categories plus at least 1 additional eligible apps ( 6 apps minimum ).
- Provide 2 financial documents you created yourself .
- Data must be genuine, recent (newest transaction within 60 days ) and cover the same 12-month period .
- Upload and validate your files through Peak Talent , with guidance from Prolific.
 Files are redacted on your own device before upload . You will never provide passwords, account credentials, or live access to your financial accounts.
 What You’ll Bring 
- US resident, 18+ 
- Access to your own eligible financial accounts and data.
- Comfortable downloading and uploading files.
- Able to follow instructions and provide your own genuine data.
 Screenshots, synthetic or AI-generated data, and scraped data are not accepted.
 You’ll first complete a short eligibility screener .
 Pay 
 $10 for the eligibility screener.
 If you pass, you’ll be invited to a separate study where you can earn $240 once your submission is reviewed and approved

 Joining our platform as a Prolific participant will give you the chance to influence the AI models of the future using your language expertise.
